stories.title: Update: Jamia keeps classes online until 8 November; two hunger strikers get final warning, police reported to have detained about 40 students
stories.body: Outlook India reported on Tuesday 27 October that Jamia Millia Islamia will keep classes online until Sunday 8 November, with the second mid-term exams also online, after a meeting chaired by Vice-Chancellor Mazhar Asif. The university will reassess the campus situation after that date. The report says two students on hunger strike were given a last warning on Monday 26 October to leave the protest site, with legal and disciplinary steps to follow. They say they will continue until a firm timeline is set. The students want the union constitution approved by Sunday 20 December and polls within 15 days; the university's order sets no approval deadline. Outlook also reports police detained at least 40 students outside the university, who were released that night from Okhla Industrial Police Station.
stories.check: NEEDS CHECK: India TV (26 Oct) says the hunger strike was called off, while Outlook and The Morning Voice (27 Oct) say two students continue; Outlook counts day 15, The Morning Voice day 12. The detention figure is from Outlook alone and is not attributed to Delhi Police. Confirm with Delhi Police and Jamia.

stories.title: Jamia teachers criticise outside political interference on campus in press release
stories.body: A Jamia Millia Islamia press release dated Tuesday 27 October says teachers, deans, heads of departments and senior officials met on Monday 26 October to review the campus situation, the length of online classes and student demands. The release calls the administration's 26 October order, which allows union elections 15 days after the constitution is approved, the first concrete step toward restoring the union since its dissolution in 2006. It says the constitution committee formed on Wednesday 21 October needs time to review court orders and ordinances. It also says an FIR was filed on Sunday 25 October over unauthorised campus entries by political leaders, and that outsiders have occupied a building block since Saturday 24 October.
stories.check: Single source, and the account is the university's: the release's claims about the entries, the occupation and the FIR were not independently confirmed, and students' response was not found. The release says online classes run until the Diwali holidays, while Outlook reports 8 November; confirm the date with Jamia. Details come from the English PDF; the release page shows only the headline.

CV Raman Marg Daily Brief, Wed 28 Oct

Jamia: classes stay online until Sun 8 Nov and mid-term exams will be online, Outlook reported on Tue 27 Oct. Two hunger strikers got a final warning to leave the protest site; Outlook also says police detained about 40 students, later released. Reports differ on whether the strike has ended.

Jamia teachers' release of 27 Oct criticises outside political interference and backs the 26 Oct union-poll order.
